steps.note: Heap sort has two phases. First turn the array into a max-heap (every parent ≥ its children); then repeatedly swap the root — the maximum — to the end and sink the new root back down.
Phase 1: build the max-heap, sifting down from the last parent up to the root.
Build: 3 was smaller than its child 9 — swap so the larger value rises.
Build: 5 was smaller than its child 9 — swap so the larger value rises.
The array is now a max-heap — the largest value, 9, sits at the front. Phase 2: extract it to the back, shrink, repeat.
Swap the max 9 into its final place at index 6. The sorted suffix now holds 1 value(s).
Re-heap: 7 was smaller than its child 8 — swap so the larger value rises.
Swap the max 8 into its final place at index 5. The sorted suffix now holds 2 value(s).
Re-heap: 2 was smaller than its child 7 — swap so the larger value rises.
Swap the max 7 into its final place at index 4. The sorted suffix now holds 3 value(s).
Re-heap: 3 was smaller than its child 5 — swap so the larger value rises.
Swap the max 5 into its final place at index 3. The sorted suffix now holds 4 value(s).
Re-heap: 1 was smaller than its child 3 — swap so the larger value rises.
Swap the max 3 into its final place at index 2. The sorted suffix now holds 5 value(s).
Swap the max 2 into its final place at index 1. The sorted suffix now holds 6 value(s).
Every value has marched into the sorted suffix: [1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 5.0, 7.0, 8.0, 9.0]. Build is O(n), each of the 6 sift-downs is O(log n) — O(n log n) total, and not one byte of extra memory.
